newsitem.title: CYPRUS: European official urges talks in divided Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: European official urges talks in divided Cyprus.

text.p: A senior European Union official called on Thursday on rival sides of divided Cyprus to embark on talks to find a political settlement to the dispute which has kept them apart for decades.

European External Affairs Commissioner Hans Van Den Broek made the call as he started a round of contacts on both sides of the divided eastern Mediterranean island, partitioned between the Turkish and Greek Cypriot communities since 1974.

"I think that now President Clerides with the leader of the Turkish Cypriot community have to embark on comprehensive talks that look at a comprehensive solution," Van Den Broek said after an hour-long meeting with Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides.

Greece, and to a lesser extent the Greek Cypriots, have reacted angrily to a push by the union this week to include a phrase calling for participation of Turkish Cypriots in a statement on the island's talks to join the EU, due to start next year.

"I confirmed the commitment of the European Union...to start accession talks next year and underlined how important it is that some perspective, some movement also on the political side would make the negotiations so much easier and we could conclude so much sooner," the EU official added.

Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded its north in 1974 in response to a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military ruling Greece at the time. The Greek Cypriot government in the south is internationally recognised as the island's only administration. The Turkish Cypriots declared their own state in the north in 1983, which is recognised only by Ankara.

Greece has threatened to block EU enlargement to the east if its European partners pressed further to include Turkish Cypriots in accession talks, but Van Den Broek said most EU states want to see the Turkish Cypriots involved.
"That does not mean that can be the case without any advance in the political process as such. It was clearly indicated that we view only a happy Cyprus as a united Cyprus...
"Obviously the north has to take its own initiative to make this possible," he added.

International mediators have recently pushed the Cyprus dispute up on the agenda of pending issues that need to be solved while it continues to remain a source of tension between NATO partners Greece and Turkey.
"If there is and remains a separation, the country will be in for constant conflict and there will be others, outside the country, benefiting from this situation," Van Den Broek warned.
